summary.headline: Vardhman Q2 FY27: yarn business recovered on higher prices and trading gains, while fabric fell YoY and QoQ on export weakness and ~20% higher input costs.
summary.overview: Management described Q2 FY27 as better than Q1 and the prior year, led by the yarn business, where yarn prices rose on export demand and higher cotton costs. Part of the yarn gain came from trading gains on cotton bought at about Rs 54-55k/candy that was later valued near Rs 64-65k/candy. Fabric was weak: top line and bottom line fell YoY and QoQ, with lower export volumes, a ~20% YoY rise in input costs, and limited pass-through. The performance fabric (synthetics) unit, commissioned in March, is still ramping and is guided to turn operating-positive in H2 FY27. Management also laid out long-term margin and growth guidance and gave a cautious view on new cotton-season prices.

segments.name: Yarn (spinning)
segments.commentary: Better performance on demand from exports and higher yarn prices, plus operational gains from recent modernisation and trading gains on cotton. Management said the trading gain may not repeat as new-season cotton costs are higher. Spinning utilisation is near 100%, with about Rs 500 crore of capex due in the next 6 months.

segments.name: Fabric (natural / processed)
segments.commentary: Weak quarter: lower export volumes amid US tariff uncertainty, domestic pricing pressure, and a 25%+ rise in processing capacity still being absorbed, so fixed-cost absorption was low. Management expects a better order pipeline after the US election, with some July orders delayed by 1-2 months.

segments.name: Performance / technical fabric (synthetics)
segments.commentary: Commissioned March; Q1 and Q2 focused on sampling, approvals and audits. Two customers have approved the plant and started orders, with utilisation at 35-40% and breakeven expected at about 50%. Management expects operating-positive in H2 FY27 and is working on defence developments.

segments.name: Government / cotton-related business
segments.commentary: Small business with about Rs 150 crore top line, running at about 7,000 units per day, currently being doubled. Management targets EBITDA rising from 7-8% to 13-14% over time.

guidance_outlook: Long-term Indian spinning EBITDA margin guidance of 16-20% (earlier 18-22%).
Long-term revenue growth of 5-8% a year, with 6-7% historically over 10 years.
Synthetics business expected to turn operating-positive in H2 FY27; expansion decision deferred until stable utilisation and product mix are reached.
Fabric utilisation expected to reach 90-95% in a few quarters; management also expects the next 6-9 months to be better for fabric.
Yarn: management expects a conversion cost of 80-90 US cents/lb to sustain, with the trading gain unlikely to recur at the same level.
capex_capacity: One spinning project under construction (about 50 tonnes/day, ~8% organic growth) due in 6-7 months; capacity for new plants is about 100,000 spindles at over Rs 1,000 crore, with 12-14 months to build.
Land at the MP Mitra Park site is expected from Nov-Dec 2026, delayed 8-9 months; management is wary of announcing a major new spinning project before land is handed over and board approval is given.
Renewable power and modernisation: about 40-50% of decided projects are complete; the rest is expected in the next 3-4 months, with savings of Rs 1-1.5/kWh.
Processing capacity for natural fabric expanded by over 25% over the past year and is still being utilised.
Performance fabric capacity was commissioned in March and is ramping up.
demand_pricing: Cotton: new-crop Indian cotton is priced around Rs 64-65k/candy (converted), against Rs 54-55k/candy when stocks were bought. Management expects no major fall in Indian cotton costs while ICE futures stay at 75-85 cents/lb.

Cotton: management expects India's crop at 28-29 million bales against consumption of 35-36 million bales, which could keep domestic prices firm; duty-free import window to Dec 31 seen as too short to matter.
Yarn export demand: China buys about 20-25 million kg/month of yarn from India; management attributes this to Chinese buyers avoiding Xinjiang cotton risk.
Industry capacity: Indian spinning capacity fell by about 12 million spindles (from 52-53 million to about 40-41 million) over three years, supporting yarn pricing.
Fabric export demand: customers have delayed orders by 1-2 months because of tariff uncertainty; pipeline is improving, with expansion into Europe and Australia.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for cotton prices and the duty-free import window?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Indian price is linked to ICE futures and is around Rs 65k/candy. The Dec 31 duty-free window is too short to bring in large volumes, so Indian cotton is unlikely to fall much.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a demand-supply gap in yarn, and what investment is needed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited capacity exits of about 12 million spindles. A new 100,000-spindle plant would cost over Rs 1,000 crore, and the sector needs clarity on raw-material policy before investing.

qa_highlights.question: What is the current spinning capacity utilisation and peak revenue potential?
qa_highlights.answer: Spinning is at about 100% utilisation. The only near-term addition is about Rs 500 crore of capacity due in the next 6 months.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Bangladesh situation and how exposed is Vardhman?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said wage unrest is recurring and expected to settle around Taka 17-18k. Bangladesh takes about 30-35% of India's roughly 110 million kg/month of yarn exports.

qa_highlights.question: What is the fabric utilisation trend and peak revenue potential on current capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Utilisation was about 70-75% in Q2 and is about 80% now. Management expects 90-95% and about 25% higher revenue on current capacity, with the increase over a few quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Is M&A or inorganic growth in spinning being considered?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is open to options, but small or distressed targets have not been viable. Its stated preference is organic growth through its own land and projects.

risks_watch: Cotton cost pass-through: new-season cotton costs are higher, so the yarn trading gain may fade and margins may compress if yarn prices soften.
Fabric export recovery depends on US tariff clarity and whether delayed orders are actually placed; fabric utilisation and pricing pressure remain key monitorables.
Performance fabric breakeven (~50% utilisation) and the H2 FY27 operating-positive target.
MP Mitra Park land handover (delayed 8-9 months) gates the next large spinning expansion.
Policy on cotton imports and MSP / CCI procurement could tighten Indian raw-material availability.
summary.management_tone: Confident on yarn and the longer-term outlook, but cautious on fabric export demand and cotton-policy uncertainty. Management was candid about fabric headwinds and was guarded on expansion timing and M&A.
